Subject: Xenon capacity: staircase SLO & surge modeling

Alex / team,

Thanks again for the time this week. Attached is a first-pass throughput / latency model for the two usage profiles you described ("steady analytic" vs "burst interactive"). High-level takeaways up front:

- For your primary LLM (large 13B-like open model, 8k context), we estimate baseline sustained throughput per GPU of ~900 tokens/sec on H100 (FP16) and ~450 tokens/sec on A100-40GB when running mixed workloads (small prompt + long completion tail).
- With int8 quantization + tuned kernels, H100 throughput can improve to ~1.4k tps in the common 1-2k token completions pattern.
- To meet a p95 latency target of ~450ms for interactive routes we recommend reserving capacity equivalent to 50-60% above steady-state peak (i.e., ~1.5x steady peak) to cover short spikes and cold-cache effects.
- For contract sizing we present a "staircase" commitment: a guaranteed slab for steady traffic + burst buffer credits for predictable async peaks. The attached spreadsheet maps tokens/day -> slab counts and expected p95 under different warm-cache assumptions.

Attached: xenon_throughput_model_v1.xlsx (tokens/sec scenarios + slab calculator), xenon_commit_MAL_v1.pdf (proposal summary).

Ask: Can you confirm the percent of traffic that will be interactive (<2s target) vs. backend batch (tolerant of 1-2s extra latency)? That split materially changes recommended reserved slabs.

If it helps, we can run a short 72-hr pilot with a canary slab and sample traffic to validate the model — we typically capture real token distribution and adjust headroom to 30-70% depending on burstiness.

Thanks,
Ben
--

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Xenon capacity: staircase SLO & surge modeling -- sizing ask from client

Ben / team,

Rolled up the numbers from the spreadsheet into two sizing options. Summary below (assumes H100-equivalent performance unless noted):

Option A (Conservative, 50% headroom):
- Steady tokens/day: 180M -> steady peak tokens/sec (estimated) = 180M / (24*3600) ≈ 2083 tokens/sec sustained.
- With 70% interactive, interactive sustained = 1458 tps.
- H100 sustained per GPU (FP16 baseline): ~900 tps -> required steady GPUs = ceil(1458 / 900) = 2 GPUs (but we add slab minimum of 4 GPUs for redundancy/throughput slices).
- For 3-4x spike handling within headroom, we recommend burst buffer equivalent to +3 GPUs (credit-based) and a reserved slab of 4 GPUs.
- Expected p95 (interactive): ~420-520ms (depends on cache warmness); batch p95 < 1.2s.

Option B (Aggressive, 30% headroom + quantized fallback):
- Same baseline; headroom tuned to 30% reduces reserved slab to 3 GPUs with 2 GPUs burst credits.
- Quantized int8 variant fallback (lower mem footprint) can increase per-GPU tps to ~1.3k, allowing temporary absorb of spikes but at slightly higher risk to output quality.
- Expected p95 (interactive): ~380-480ms when cache warmed; batch p95 < 900ms under normal burst credits.

Operational notes and playbook:
- Warm cache: keep a small prefix cache on each slab; recommend 10-15 minute warm-up for cache-sensitive prompts (we also include a TTL-based pre-warm for planned launches).
- Autoscale policy: scale-up trigger at 75% aggregate token-utilization across the slab; scale-down after a 20 minute cool-off to avoid thrash.
- Fallbacks: route to quantized variant automatically when GPU utilization > 90% for >60s; provide per-route quality SLA exemptions for fallbacks in contract language.
- Canary run recommended: provision 1 test slab (2 GPUs) for 72 hours and collect real token distribution to refine headroom.

I'll attach a one-page table (sent as a stub) with the slab math and expected p95 ranges.

-Karthik

Attachments: k8s-autoscale-profiles.json (policy stubs), sizing_onepager.pdf (stub)
